tasks.description: Read in/settings.txt. On every line remove everything from the first '#' to the end of the line, then remove trailing spaces. Drop lines that are empty or only spaces after that. Write the remaining lines to out/result.txt in order.

inputs.in/settings.txt:
# settings
host = example.org  # primary

port = 8080
   # indented comment

release notes for march
known issues
upgrade guide and faq

Release Notes For March

tasks.description: Read in/ledger.csv (header date,account,amount; comma-separated, no quoting; amount is a signed integer). Write out/result.json: an object mapping each account to its integer balance (sum of its amounts).
Read in/ledger.csv. Write out/result.json: an object mapping each month (the first 7 characters of date, YYYY-MM) to the integer sum of amounts in that month.

Read in/lines.csv (header item,qty,unit; integers for qty and unit). Write out/result.csv: the same table with a fourth column named total equal to qty * unit, header included, rows in input order, comma-separated.
Read in/team.csv (header name,role). Write out/result.txt with one line per data row: the name padded on the right with spaces to the length of the longest name, then " | ", then the role.
tasks.expected:
Annika      | lead
Bo          | dev
Christopher | dev
Dee         | qa

tasks.description: Read in/latency.txt (one integer per line; the count is odd). Write out/result.txt with the median value.
Read in/seconds.txt (one non-negative integer per line). Write out/result.txt with each value as H:MM:SS (hours not padded, minutes and seconds two digits), one per line.

Read in/ages.txt (one line of comma-separated non-negative integers). Bucket them by tens. Write out/result.txt with one line per non-empty bucket in ascending order, formatted "<lo>-<hi>: <count>" (e.g. "10-19: 2").
Read in/load.txt (one line of comma-separated integers). Write out/result.json: the JSON array of 3-wide moving averages, each rounded down (floor), one per full window, in order.
Read in/jobs.json (array of strings). Write out/result.json: the elements split into consecutive batches of 3 (the last batch may be shorter), as an array of arrays.

Read in/left.json and in/right.json (arrays of strings). Write out/result.json: their elements interleaved (left[0], right[0], left[1], right[1], ...); when one runs out, append the rest of the other.
Read in/ring.json (array of strings) and in/k.txt (one non-negative integer k). Write out/result.json: the array rotated left by k positions (k may exceed the length; rotation wraps).
Read in/meter.json (array of integers, cumulative meter readings). Write out/result.json: the array of differences between each reading and the one before it (one element shorter than the input).
Read in/raw.txt (one line). Run-length encode it: each maximal run of the same character becomes the character followed by the run length (e.g. "aab" -> "a2b1"). Write it to out/result.txt.

Read in/idents.txt (one camelCase identifier per line, starting lower-case). Write out/result.txt with each converted to snake_case (insert '_' before every upper-case letter and lower-case it), one per line.
Read in/msg.txt (one line). Shift every lower-case letter a-z forward by 3 places in the alphabet, wrapping z to c; leave every other character unchanged. Write it to out/result.txt.
Read in/cards.txt (one digit string per line). Write out/result.txt with each line masked: every character except the last 4 replaced by '*'.

Read in/staff.json (array of {name, manager}; manager is "" for the top). Write out/result.json: an object mapping each manager who has at least one report to the array of their direct reports' names in input order.

Read in/users.json (array of {id, name}) and in/scores.json (array of {user, points}; user is a user id). Write out/result.txt with one line per user in users.json order: "<name> <total points>" (0 if the user has no scores).

Read in/stock.json (object of sku to integer count) and in/moves.json (array of {sku, delta}). Apply every move in order (a sku not yet in stock starts at 0). Write out/result.json: the final stock object.
Read in/carts.json (array of {cart, items}; items is an array of {sku, qty}). Write out/result.json: an object mapping each sku to its total integer qty across all carts.
Read in/n.txt (one integer n >= 2). Write out/result.txt with all primes p <= n separated by single spaces, ascending.
Read in/n.txt (one integer n >= 1). Repeatedly replace n by n/2 if it is even or 3n+1 if it is odd, until n is 1. Write out/result.txt with the integer number of steps taken.

Read in/years.txt (one integer year per line). Write out/result.txt with one line per year: "<year> leap" or "<year> common" (Gregorian rules: divisible by 4, except centuries unless divisible by 400).
tasks.expected:
1900 common
2000 leap
2024 leap
2023 common
2100 common
2400 leap

tasks.description: Read in/cmds.txt (one command per line). A door starts "closed". Allowed transitions: closed+open->opened, opened+close->closed, closed+lock->locked, locked+unlock->closed. Process commands in order; at the first command not allowed in the current state stop and write "error line <n>: cannot <cmd> when <state>" (n is 1-based). If all succeed, write the final state. Output goes to out/result.txt.
tasks.expected: error line 4: cannot open when locked

tasks.description: Read in/spend.txt (one integer per line) and in/budget.txt (one integer). Add the values in order; write out/result.txt with "over at <n>" for the 1-based line where the running total first exceeds the budget, or "within budget" if it never does.
Read in/romans.txt (one valid Roman numeral per line, I V X L C D M with subtractive forms). Write out/result.json: the JSON array of their integer values in order.
Read in/nums.txt (one non-negative integer per line). Write out/result.txt with each number in base 2 (no prefix, "0" for zero), one per line.

Read in/ids.txt (one digit string per line). Write out/result.txt with "<digits> valid" or "<digits> invalid" per line according to the Luhn checksum (from the rightmost digit, double every second digit, subtract 9 from results over 9, sum all; valid if the sum is divisible by 10).

Read in/board.json (array of {name, score}). Sort by score descending, then name ascending. Write out/result.txt with one line per entry "<rank> <name> <score>" using dense ranking (equal scores share a rank; the next distinct score gets the next rank).
tasks.expected:
1 ari 95
1 lou 95
2 kim 88
2 zed 88
3 max 81
4 bea 70

tasks.description: Read in/maze.txt (rows of '#', '.' and exactly one 'S'). Write out/result.txt with "<row>,<col> <walls>": the 0-based row and column of 'S' and the number of '#' cells directly up, down, left or right of it (cells off the grid do not count).

Read in/prices.json (array of integers) and in/target.txt (one integer). Find the pair of 0-based indices i < j with prices[i] + prices[j] == target that has the smallest j (then the smallest i). Write "<i> <j>" to out/result.txt, or "none" if no pair exists.

Read in/passwords.txt (one per line). For each, write the first failing rule, checked in this order: "too short" if fewer than 8 characters, "no digit" if it has no 0-9, "no upper" if it has no A-Z; otherwise "ok". One result per line in out/result.txt.
tasks.expected:
too short
no digit
no upper
ok
too short

tasks.description: Read in/board.txt (3 lines of 3 characters, each 'X', 'O' or '.'). Write out/result.txt with "X" or "O" if that player has three in a row (row, column or diagonal), else "draw" if no '.' remains, else "open". At most one player has a line.
